title: Coffee Disturbs Sleep in Ways We May Not Notice
paragraphs: Some people have one coffee before noon and still find themselves lying wide awake in bed hours later. Others can finish a cup after dinner and fall asleep as usual.
But does falling asleep easily mean caffeine isn't affecting your sleep?
New research says the answer is "no."
Researchers from Poland looked at 32 earlier studies on caffeine and brain activity during sleep. The participants were healthy adults who usually had one to three caffeinated drinks a day.
The studies all looked at electrical activity in people's brains as they slept.

Across the studies, caffeine was consistently linked to less of the "slow-wave" brain activity usually seen during deep sleep — an important stage for rest and keeping the brain healthy. At the same time, there was often more "fast" brain activity, making sleep lighter and less restful.
These changes were greater or smaller depending on things like how much caffeine people had, when they had it, and how often they usually had it.

But these changes appeared even when people slept for the same amount of time as usual. So, you might fall asleep easily and get your usual hours after a cup of coffee, but that caffeine is still affecting the quality of your sleep.
And while caffeine can make you feel more awake during the day, if your sleep that night is less restful, you may wake up feeling tired the next day — which makes you reach for even more caffeine.
However, the researchers say the effect isn't the same for everyone — for some people, even coffee earlier in the day may disturb their sleep at night, for example.
"Caffeine is neither 'good' nor 'bad'," study author Donata Kurpas said. What matters is how much you have, when you have it and how your body responds to it.
